documents.doc_summary: User manual for TaskFlow Pro 4.2, a team project management tool, covering system requirements, installation, the dashboard, project creation, member roles, task assignment, reporting and settings. It closes with configuration of user preferences and third-party integrations such as Slack, GitHub and Google Calendar.

sections.title: user_manual.docx
sections.summary: User manual for TaskFlow Pro 4.2, a team project management tool, covering system requirements, installation, the dashboard, project creation, member roles, task assignment, reporting and settings. It closes with configuration of user preferences and third-party integrations such as Slack, GitHub and Google Calendar.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Introduces TaskFlow Pro 4.2, describing what the product does, the system requirements, and how to install it.

sections.title: About
sections.summary: TaskFlow Pro is a web and desktop project management tool for teams of 5-500 that combines Kanban boards, Gantt timelines, time tracking and reporting.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.summary: Lists supported browsers, desktop OS versions, minimum hardware (4 GB RAM, dual-core CPU) and network requirements for TaskFlow Pro.

sections.title: Installation
sections.summary: Explains how to access the web version, install the desktop client via the installer, and sign in for the first time using SSO or email.

sections.title: Features
sections.summary: Describes the core features of TaskFlow Pro: the dashboard, project management workflows, reports and settings.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.summary: The dashboard is the landing page that summarises a user's projects, tasks and team activity.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: The dashboard shows four KPI cards (active projects, open tasks, due this week, overdue), a weekly completion chart and a recent activity feed (see figure_000.png).

sections.title: Navigation
sections.summary: Covers the left sidebar menu, the global search box, and keyboard shortcuts such as Ctrl+K for search and G then P for projects.

sections.title: Project Management
sections.summary: Explains how to create projects, add team members with roles, and assign tasks.

sections.title: Creating a Project
sections.summary: Projects are created from Projects > New Project by entering a name, unique key, template, dates and visibility (see figure_001.png).

sections.title: Adding Team Members
sections.summary: Members are invited from Project > Members by email and assigned one of four roles: Owner, Manager, Contributor or Viewer.

sections.title: Task Assignment
sections.summary: Tasks are assigned via the Assignee field or by dragging onto a member's avatar; workload view warns when a member exceeds 40 hours per week.

sections.title: Reports
sections.summary: Describes built-in reports - burndown, velocity, time tracking and overdue tasks - and export to PDF/CSV (see figure_002.png).

sections.title: Settings
sections.summary: Settings covers profile details, notification channels, security options such as two-factor authentication, and workspace administration for admins.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.summary: Covers configuring personal preferences and connecting third-party integrations.

sections.title: User Preferences
sections.summary: Users can set theme, language, time zone, start of week, date format and default board view from Settings > Profile.

sections.title: Integrations
sections.summary: Lists supported integrations (Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, GitLab, Google Calendar, Jira import) and how admins connect them with OAuth.

documents.doc_summary: Acme Technologies' HR leave policy (HR-POL-007 v3.1) defining entitlements for privilege, casual/sick, maternity/paternity, marriage, compassionate, award and medical checkup leave. It also sets out the HRMS-based approval workflow, the annual holiday list and an annexure of abbreviations.

sections.title: leave_policy.pdf
sections.summary: Acme Technologies' HR leave policy (HR-POL-007 v3.1) defining entitlements for privilege, casual/sick, maternity/paternity, marriage, compassionate, award and medical checkup leave. It also sets out the HRMS-based approval workflow, the annual holiday list and an annexure of abbreviations.

sections.title: LEAVE POLICY
sections.summary: Title block of Acme Technologies' leave policy, document HR-POL-007 version 3.1, effective 1 April 2026.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope:
sections.summary: Defines the purpose of providing employees with structured time off and states the policy applies to all permanent and probationary employees in India.

sections.title: Policy:
sections.summary: States that the leave year runs January-December, leave accrues monthly, and all leave must be applied for through the HRMS portal.

sections.title: A. Privilege Leave & Casual / Sick Leave
sections.summary: Employees receive 18 days privilege leave (max 45 carried forward) and 12 days casual/sick leave (not carried forward); sick leave over 2 days needs a medical certificate.

sections.title: B. Maternity / Paternity Leave
sections.summary: Female employees receive 26 weeks paid maternity leave for the first two children (12 weeks thereafter); fathers get 10 working days paternity leave within 3 months of birth.

sections.title: C. Marriage And Compassionate Leave
sections.summary: Grants 5 working days marriage leave once during employment and 5 days compassionate leave on the death of an immediate family member.

sections.title: D. Award Leave
sections.summary: Employees recognised in the annual awards or completing 5/10 years of service receive 2-5 additional days of award leave to be used within 6 months.

sections.title: E. Official Medical Checkup Leave
sections.summary: Employees aged 35 and above get one day of paid leave per year for the company-sponsored annual health checkup.

sections.title: Leave Approval Procedure
sections.summary: Leave is applied on HRMS, reviewed by the reporting manager within 2 working days, escalated to the HOD if over 5 days, then recorded by HR (see figure_000.png).

sections.title: HOLIDAYS
sections.summary: The company observes 10 paid public holidays per year (8 fixed national/festival holidays plus 2 optional holidays chosen by the employee); the list is published each December.

sections.title: ANNEXURE
sections.summary: Contains the leave summary table and abbreviations (PL, CL/SL, LWP, HOD, HRMS) used throughout the policy.

documents.doc_summary: IntelliJ-style project code style configuration (scheme 'Project', version 173) stored as XML. It enables spaces inside empty HTML tags and enforced attribute quotes, and for JavaScript forces semicolons and disables the space before function parentheses.

sections.title: config.xml
sections.summary: IntelliJ-style project code style configuration (scheme 'Project', version 173) stored as XML. It enables spaces inside empty HTML tags and enforced attribute quotes, and for JavaScript forces semicolons and disables the space before function parentheses.

sections.title: <component name="ProjectCodeStyleConfiguration">
sections.summary: Root IntelliJ component that stores the project-level code style configuration.

sections.title: <code_scheme name="Project" version="173">
sections.summary: Opens the shared 'Project' code scheme, format version 173, applied to all project files.

sections.title: <HTMLCodeStyleSettings>
sections.summary: Begins the block of HTML formatter settings.

sections.title: <option name="HTML_SPACE_INSIDE_EMPTY_TAG" value="true" />
sections.summary:
Inserts a space before the closing slash of empty tags, e.g.
.

sections.title: <option name="HTML_ENFORCE_QUOTES" value="true" />
sections.summary: Forces attribute values to be wrapped in quotes.

sections.title: </HTMLCodeStyleSettings>
sections.summary: Ends the HTML formatter settings block.

sections.title: <JSCodeStyleSettings>
sections.summary: Begins the block of JavaScript formatter settings.

sections.title: <option name="FORCE_SEMICOLON_STYLE" value="true" />
sections.summary: Enforces the configured semicolon style, adding statement-terminating semicolons on reformat.

sections.title: <option name="SPACE_BEFORE_FUNCTION_LEFT_PARENTH" value="false" />
sections.summary: No space between a function name and its opening parenthesis: function foo() rather than function foo ().

sections.title: </JSCodeStyleSettings>
sections.summary: Ends the JavaScript formatter settings block.

sections.title: </code_scheme>
sections.summary: Closes the Project code scheme.

sections.title: </component>
sections.summary: Closes the ProjectCodeStyleConfiguration component.

documents.doc_summary: Pinned pip requirements for a small FastAPI web API using PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy, Alembic and psycopg, with JWT auth through python-jose and passlib. It separates core runtime packages from development tooling (pytest, ruff, mypy) and pins httpx as the HTTP client.
